request: I fly to Singapore on 31 January for the urban rail congress, which opens on 2 February. Economy is fine and so is the overnight flight; I'll ask for the rest day the guide allows after such a long flight.

sign_offs.name: Head of unit
sign_offs.subject: MISSION_ORDER
sign_offs.note: Mission order signed: purpose, dates and place of the mission

sign_offs.name: Authorising officer
sign_offs.subject: MISSION_ORDER
sign_offs.note: Mission order signed for the budget: the mission's cost estimate

must_keep.quote: As a general rule, you can book air travel: a) in economy class or equivalent, including cases where the ticket in question cannot be exchanged or refunded, at the lowest available rates, taking into account the times of meetings and/or special features of the mission;
must_keep.why: (a) economy, including non-refundable, at the lowest available rates

must_keep.quote: Air travel for distances up to 550 km must be appropriately justified (40), and direct flights favoured when available, and within reasonable cost variations (40%). Economy class remains the default option.
must_keep.why: air up to 550 km must be justified; direct flights favoured within 40%; economy the default

distractors.quote: if the total duration of the flights is at least 10 hours, the authorising officer for commitments may decide to grant the mission performer a rest period of up to 24 hours before the meetings
distractors.why: a rest period after long flights, granted by the authorising officer; not a ticket rule

distractors.quote: more than 6 hours but not more than 12 hours: 50% of the daily allowance
distractors.why: daily allowance hours, not flight hours

design_notes: Business or premium economy would be allowed (a 760-775 minute segment, lines 707-710), but the traveller asks for economy: the lowest fare, Singapore Airlines 12:40 at EUR 695, landing on 1 February. The rest period after at least 10 hours of flights (lines 815-818) is for the authorising officer to grant at the destination; it changes no ticket.
